displayName: RACGP — Standards for General Practices & Clinical Guidelines

chunks.heading: Purpose of the Standards
chunks.text: The RACGP developed the Standards with a clear mission: protecting patients from harm by improving the quality and safety of health services. Beyond patient protection, these standards serve as a diagnostic tool, helping practices identify and address any gaps in their systems and processes.
chunks.sourceTitle: Introduction to the Standards for General Practice (5th edition)

chunks.heading: Core Module (8 Standards)
chunks.text: Establishes foundational requirements covering communication, patient rights, governance, health promotion, clinical management, information systems, record content, and staff training.
chunks.sourceTitle: Introduction to the Standards for General Practice (5th edition)

chunks.heading: Quality Improvement Module (3 Standards)
chunks.text: Focuses on continuous enhancement through quality activities, clinical indicators, and risk management practices including open disclosure protocols.
chunks.sourceTitle: Introduction to the Standards for General Practice (5th edition)

chunks.heading: General Practice Module (6 Standards)
chunks.text: Addresses access to care, comprehensive service delivery, clinical team qualifications, infection prevention, physical facilities/equipment, and vaccine management.
chunks.sourceTitle: Introduction to the Standards for General Practice (5th edition)

chunks.heading: Specialised modules
chunks.text: Additional standards exist for after-hours services, medical deputising, point-of-care testing, and various healthcare settings including aged care and detention facilities.
chunks.sourceTitle: Introduction to the Standards for General Practice (5th edition)

chunks.heading: Clinical guidelines overview
chunks.text: RACGP produces or endorses guidelines organised by topic covering preventative care and clinical areas, including the National Guide for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander preventive healthcare and type 2 diabetes management. The Handbook of Non-Drug Interventions (HANDI) is an online formulary of non-drug interventions, enabling GPs to offer patients a greater choice of interventions. "First Do No Harm" is an evidence-based resource assisting GP and patient conversations on overused tests, overdiagnosed and overtreated conditions. The Abuse and Violence Guidelines are a practical resource for health practitioners.
